newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan merges, to privatise publishing houses.
newsitem.headline: Sudan merges, to privatise publishing houses.

text.p: Sudan has merged its three state-owned publishing houses into a single firm which it will float on the Khartoum stock exchange, the official Sudan News Agency (SUNA) reported on Friday.

SUNA said the government incorporated on Thursday Sudan House, Dar al-Ingaz and Dar al-Sudan al-Hadith, appointing a temporary state-dominated board of directors to evaluate the new firm and prepare it for privatisation.
Amin Hassan Omar, press advisor to Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, will head the new firm and the state will provide funding until it can support itself, SUNA reported.

The agency quoted Omar as saying that the aim of the new company is to allow broad-based ownership of the press and to better its performance. Sudan has several privately-owned newspapers and publishing houses.
